seo.title: Zangla Excursion — 4½ Days from Leh into Zanskar | Adventure Access
seo.description: A short trip from Leh: Nimmu House, Zangla's royal palace, a stronghold hike and a riverside trail to Hanamur. From $1,889, double occupancy.

hero.title: Zangla
hero.subtitle: A short, full trip from Leh to Zanskar's old palace town, with a royal stronghold hike and a night in a riverside village
hero.imageAlt: A hiker on a trail through a dry canyon

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Shorter, Not Soft
paragraphs: A day in Zanskar can take you from rugged ridgelines to sparkling blue pools to a cozy homestay. This itinerary is shorter and slightly easier than our other trips, but these trails are not easy, and hiking at this altitude will still give you a real challenge on some of the highest trails in the world.

Zanskar's culture has stayed mostly unchanged for a thousand years, so much of this trip is spent with Ladakhi people and in their homes. Our local specialists handle everything from pickup to drop-off, so you can focus on the trip.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Rest, Drive, Hike, Return
dayTypes.lede: With altitudes pushing 16,000 feet in the region, we ease into activity. The first day is for rest, food and a gentle village walk.

cards.title: Rest day
cards.body: Day 1: straight from Leh to Nimmu House for rest, good food and a guided walk through the old village.

cards.title: Zanskar days
cards.body: Days 2–3: the drive deep into the mountains, Zangla Palace, a steep stronghold hike with water crossings, and a riverside trail to Hanamur.

cards.title: Leh
cards.body: Days 4–5: the drive back, an evening in Leh's markets or up to Shanti Stupa, a celebration dinner, then the airport.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Four and a Half Days in Zanskar
chapters.lede: Hike figures are distance, total ascent and highest point.

groups.title: Nimmu — Rest at a Village Home

image.alt: Lounge chairs inside a tent at Nimmu House, looking onto a stone courtyard

prose: Nimmu House is a traditional Ladakhi home, still lived in, that has been turned into a small hotel with excellent food. Its courtyards, luxury tents and comfortable rooms are a first way into the history and culture of the region.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Pickup in Leh and straight to Nimmu. Rest and good food, then a guided walk through the old village for a look at Ladakhi life as it has been for a thousand years.

groups.title: Into Zanskar — The Palace Town of Zangla

image.alt: A white 4x4 on a gravel mountain road

prose: The drive is an adventure in itself: deep into the mountains along the Zanskar River, past tiny villages and wildly twisting rock. At the end is Zangla, whose palace was home to the king of Zanskar until recently.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: Breakfast at Nimmu House, then the long drive to a homestay in Zangla. Tea and lunch, then up to Zangla Palace to explore it freely. An evening of food and local stories.

groups.title: Zangla and Hanamur — Stronghold and River Trail

image.alt: Hikers on the trail toward the chortens below Zangla palace

prose: Two hikes in one day. In the morning, steep terrain and water crossings that were meant to protect a royal stronghold in the mountains behind Zangla. In the afternoon, a few hours on a riverside trail to the remote village of Hanamur.

tracks.name: Ancient Palace hike
tracks.text: A challenging hike to the old royal stronghold, then lunch with your host family. 5.2 mi · 1,857 ft up · high point 11,962 ft.

tracks.name: Pidmo to Hanamur
tracks.text: Drive to the trailhead and walk the river to Hanamur for an evening under the stars with a homestay family. 3.8 mi · 456 ft up · high point 11,286 ft.

groups.title: Leh — Markets, Stories and the Flight Out

image.alt: Leh old town with prayer flags and the palace above

prose: Leh feels like an overgrown village with busy streets, market alleys and great food. After Zanskar it can feel like a metropolis.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: Hike back from Hanamur, then about five hours on the road to Leh. Explore the old market streets and the Central Asian Museum, or hike to Shanti Stupa for views over town. A celebration dinner to share the best stories.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: A taxi to Leh airport in the morning, in Delhi by the afternoon. Ask us if you want to add more time in Ladakh or Delhi.

pullQuote: From rugged ridgelines to sparkling blue pools and cozy homestays, all in a few hours.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Fitness
cards.body: Shorter and slightly easier than our other trips, but the stronghold hike is steep, with water crossings, and the altitude will still push you.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: The palace hike tops out at 11,962 feet. We ease into activity, and your guides pay close attention to acclimatization.

cards.title: Local culture
cards.body: Ladakhi culture is very hospitable. Your guide will keep you informed on local customs as you go. Learn as you travel, and leave better than you came.

cards.title: Water and the land
cards.body: Instead of hundreds of plastic bottles, we provide a more sustainable way to keep you supplied with clean water, and we take our cues from local partners on how to travel well here.

cards.title: Where your money goes
cards.body: We give 3% of general revenue to sponsor children in Zanskar, so they can go to school.

cards.title: Living in India?
cards.body: Reach out to info@adventure-access.com for a modified itinerary and pricing for residents.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Village Homes and a Garden Hotel
paragraphs: Nimmu House starts the trip. Most villages in Zanskar have no hotels, so you stay in homestays, some rustic and some with more comforts. In Leh we prefer 3–4 star places with hospitable owners over glossy hotels with poor service. Omasila is a comfortable hotel in the heart of Leh, with a garden for unwinding over tea.
